summary: Generated 6 user stories, a full-stack architecture, 9 API endpoints, and PostgreSQL architecture decisions for a task-management SaaS.

requirements.user_story: As a new user, I can register and log in with email and password so that my tasks are private to me.
acceptance_criteria: POST /auth/register creates a user and returns a JWT.
POST /auth/login returns a JWT on valid credentials.
Requests without a valid JWT receive 401.

requirements.user_story: As a logged-in user, I can create a task with a title, description, and due date so that I can track my work.
acceptance_criteria: POST /tasks creates a task and returns the new task object.
Due date is stored as ISO 8601 UTC.

requirements.user_story: As a logged-in user, I can view my tasks so that I have a full picture of my workload.
acceptance_criteria: GET /tasks returns only tasks accessible to the authenticated user.
The response is a JSON array.
An empty list is returned when the user has no tasks.

requirements.user_story: As a logged-in user, I can update a task so that its information stays accurate.
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /tasks/{id} updates only the fields provided.

requirements.user_story: As a logged-in user, I can delete a task I own so that unwanted work is removed.
acceptance_criteria: DELETE /tasks/{id} removes the task and returns 204.

requirements.user_story: As a team member, I can share a task with another user so that we can collaborate.
acceptance_criteria: POST /tasks/{id}/share accepts a target user email and grants read access.
The shared user can see the task.
Only the task owner can share the task.

stack.frontend: Next.js 14 with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS

adr.question: Which database should we use?
adr.reason: Relational data with clear ownership foreign keys and ACID transaction requirements.

adr.question: How should users be authenticated?
adr.reason: Stateless authentication avoids a shared session store between frontend and backend services.

adr.question: Which frontend framework should we use?
adr.reason: File-based routing, TypeScript safety, and rapid UI iteration support the 48-hour build.
